# Gig Recorder

> Gig Recorder is a live music recording app for iPhone, iPad, and Mac. It records an
> entire gig, concert set, or rehearsal as one take, automatically splits it into
> individually named songs, and turns the night into a shareable playlist. Song naming
> is done entirely on-device against a private reference library built from the user's
> own recordings; it never uses Shazam or any public/online song database. Free to
> record, split, name, edit, Enhance, and build playlists. Gig Recorder Pro is a
> one-time $1.29 in-app purchase (no subscription) that unlocks sharing, export,
> Dropbox/iCloud sync, and custom Effects. No accounts, no tracking, no ads, and no
> servers: nothing is collected or stored for use by anyone but the user.

## Key facts
- Platforms: iPhone, iPad, Mac (Mac Catalyst), with Apple Watch remote start/stop.
- Core feature: automatic song-boundary detection that splits one long live recording
  into separate, named tracks.
- Song naming: a private, on-device, per-user reference library, not Shazam and not a
  public/online music database. It learns from names the user confirms or corrects.
- Privacy: no accounts, no analytics, no ads, no company servers. Recordings and the
  song library stay on-device unless the user opts into their own iCloud or Dropbox.
- Pricing: free core app (record, split, name, edit, one-tap Enhance, playlists);
  Gig Recorder Pro unlocks sharing, export, cloud sync, and custom Effects for a
  one-time $1.29 purchase.
- Audience: gigging bands, cover acts, solo/singer-songwriter performers, open-mic
  hosts, rehearsal-heavy groups, and (secondarily) fans at record-friendly shows.
